Section 1 of 9

Why Are You Here?

You can search almost anything in seconds. Yet some of life’s biggest questions cannot be answered by a search bar:

Why am I here?

Does my life have a purpose?

Is there really a Creator?

If He exists, does He know me?

Can I know Him without turning my back on who I am?

These are honest questions. You deserve more than shallow answers.

The Bible begins with a simple truth: you are here because the Creator wanted human life to exist. You are not an accident, a mistake, or a forgotten person. You were created with dignity, value, and the ability to know the One who gave you life.

The Creator Was Already Here

The Creator did not arrive in North America with missionaries. He was already here.

He made the land, water, sky, animals, plants, and every human family. He knew your people long before anyone crossed an ocean carrying a Bible.

People have sometimes used God’s name to control Native people, separate children from their families, silence Native languages, and create shame about Native identity. That harm was wrong. It did not reveal the heart of the Creator.

You do not have to excuse that history to explore the Bible. You do not have to become less Native to know God. Your family, nation, language, culture, and, and personal story are part of who you are.

God’s invitation is simple: come and discover who He truly is.

What Does Creation Tell Us?

Read Psalm 19:1–4 ↗ and Romans 1:20 ↗.

The sky, stars, seasons, living creatures, and the order of life point beyond themselves. They show power, wisdom, beauty, and careful design.

Creation is a sign that points toward the Creator. Creation itself is not God. The One who made the natural world is greater than everything He created.

Nature can show us that the Creator is powerful, but it cannot answer every question about His character. It cannot fully explain why suffering exists, how forgiveness works, or what happens after death.

For those answers, we need the Creator to speak.

Does the Bible Belong to One Culture?

The Bible does not belong to Europeans, Americans, or any one church. Most of its human writers came from the ancient Middle East.

The Bible was written through people who lived in particular times and cultures, but its authority stands above every culture. It even stands above religious institutions and governments that have misused its words.

Its message reaches every nation because the Creator made every nation.

The Bible does not teach that one race is more valuable, intelligent, spiritual, or human than another. It says:

“God created man in his own image.”

Genesis 1:27 ↗

Every person carries God-given value. That includes you.

Read Acts 17:24–28 ↗.

This passage teaches that God made every nation and that He is near to each of us. No group owns Him. No culture can keep Him away from another people.

You Were Created on Purpose

Read Genesis 1:26–31 ↗.

The Creator made human beings in His image. This means you were created with the ability to think, choose, love, create, build relationships, and care for the world around you.

Your value was given to you before you earned money, received a degree, started a career, built a family, or proved yourself to anyone.

Your worth comes from your Creator.

Genesis also says that God completed creation in six days. On the seventh day, He rested, blessed the day, and made it holy.

Read Genesis 2:1–3 ↗.

The first full day of human life was spent resting with the Creator. Humanity began with relationship, peace, and belonging. We did not begin by proving our worth through work.

The Creator wanted people to know Him from the beginning.

Why Does the Creator Sometimes Feel Far Away?

If God wants to know us, why can He feel so distant?

Read Isaiah 59:1–2 ↗ and Romans 3:23 ↗.

The Bible calls the problem sin. Sin is more than making occasional mistakes. It is choosing our own way over the Creator’s way. Sin damages our connection with God and harms our relationships with one another.

Every person and every society has been touched by sin. Greed, abuse, racism, violence, addiction, dishonesty, and the misuse of religion grow from humanity’s separation from God.

Yet the Creator did not abandon us.

He came looking for us.

The Creator Came Near Through Jesus

Read John 1:1–3 ↗ and John 1:14 ↗.

These verses call Jesus “the Word.” They teach that everything was created through Him and that He entered the human family.

Jesus was present at creation. He is more than a wise teacher or a religious leader. He is the Creator who came near enough to be seen, heard, and known.

Read John 14:9 ↗.

Jesus showed us what God is like. He welcomed people who had been pushed aside. He healed the hurting, confronted religious hypocrisy, defended the mistreated, forgave sin, and spoke the truth with love.

When you want to know the Creator’s heart, look at Jesus.

The same Jesus who made you chose to suffer and die for you. He rose from the dead so that sin, shame, injustice, and death would not have the final word.

You matter that much to Him.

Can You Know the Creator Personally?

Read Jeremiah 29:13 ↗ and John 17:3 ↗.

Knowing the Creator involves more than knowing facts about Him. He invites you into a real relationship built on truth, trust, prayer, and time in His Word.

You do not need perfect faith to begin. You can start with honest curiosity.

You can say:

“Creator, I am not sure what I believe. If You are there, help me know You as You truly are.”

God is not afraid of your questions.

Think About It

Take a moment and write your answers.

  1. When you hear the word “Creator,” what comes to mind?
  2. What have you been taught about God or the Bible?
  3. Has religion ever made you feel that your Native identity was unwanted or inferior?
  4. If you could ask the Creator one honest question, what would it be?
  5. Which idea from this guide stood out to you most?

Try This During the Coming Week

Set aside ten quiet minutes on three different days.

Read one passage each time:

  • Day 1: Genesis 1:1–31 ↗
  • Day 2: Psalm 19:1–6 ↗
  • Day 3: John 1:1–18 ↗

Before reading, ask the Creator to help you understand what is true.

After reading, write down:

  • What does this passage show me about the Creator?
  • What does it show me about my value?
  • What question do I still have?

There is no pressure to pretend or produce a certain answer. Begin with honesty.

A Prayer You Can Pray

Creator God, thank You for giving me life and knowing my story. Help me see You clearly. Show me what is true through Your Word and through Jesus. Heal the places where Your name has been misused. Give me wisdom as I explore these teachings. Help me understand my value, my purpose, and Your love for me. Amen.

Remember This

You are not an accident.

You were created with dignity.

No race or culture owns the Creator.

The Bible’s message is for every nation.

Jesus reveals what the Creator is truly like.

You can begin knowing Him today without surrendering who you are.
